rationale: Ninth investigation, taking up the deferred surface that recorded the commit context of a follower that installs a snapshot. The surface observed that installSnapshot publishes lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the requested index and truncates the log but never advances raftState.commitIndex, so a node that has just taken committed state as applied still reports a commit index below it. The map already carries the fact (f-commit-index: an entry at I has been stored by a quorum of the current voting configuration and may be applied to the FSM), the producing behaviour on the append path (b-follower-commit-advance), the consumer (b-client-apply-verify, which reports the value through the exported accessor and Stats) and the installing behaviour b-install-snapshot, whose recorded writes name lastApplied and lastSnapshot but not the commit index. The check is the surface's deterministic instance: a real leader commits forty entries and snapshots at index J, a second voter installs exactly that snapshot through the module's own InstallSnapshot path, and the index the installing node publishes as its commit index is compared with J while its applied and last indexes are recorded beside it.

candidate.rationale: New Candidate opened from the deferred snapshot commit-context surface. It states the publishing duty for the commit-index fact on the path that installs a committed snapshot and binds it to the installSnapshot entry point, which records the applied and snapshot indexes but not the commit index.

question.question: After a node installs a snapshot that carries state the source had committed and applied through index J, does the commit context the node publishes - Raft.CommitIndex(), which is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation - identify a commit point at least J, or can the node hold applied state at J while reporting a lower commit index?
question.importance: The published commit index is the value a server uses to implement the read-index optimisation described in the Raft paper, so a node that under-reports it cannot be used to derive a read index for the committed state it already holds, and any client or monitor that relates the reported commit point to the applied point sees applied state ahead of committed state. The state in question is not speculative: the snapshot payload is the source's committed and applied FSM state, and the receiving node adopts it wholesale. The consequence is a client-contract one rather than a safety one, but the value the node publishes is wrong for the whole window in which it holds that state without having heard an advertised commit index, and on the startup restore path it is wrong until a leader contacts the node at all.
question.trigger_rationale: The installer restores the snapshot and then publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from req.LastLogIndex, truncates the log and answers success; the commit index is written only in the appendEntries commit branch, as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), so a node whose commit index is still at its old (or zero) value keeps reporting it while already applying through the snapshot index. The source's own report of the same index as committed and applied is what makes the comparison unambiguous: within this prefix the receiver's last index becomes that index, so the requirement that the published value may not fall below it is exactly the comparison the check performs.
participants: the source node that committed and snapshotted the state
the voter that installs the snapshot
a client reading the installing node's commit index or Stats
objects: raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot written by installSnapshot
the snapshot index carried by InstallSnapshotRequest.LastLogIndex
the commit_index and applied_index entries of Raft.Stats
contexts: a voter in the source's configuration that installs the snapshot by the module's own InstallSnapshot path
the prefix immediately after the install, before any later AppendEntries advertises a commit index
event_paths: source path: Apply commits and applies entries, Snapshot persists the FSM at the applied index and compacts the log

install path: the request carries the snapshot metadata, installSnapshot copies the payload into a new sink, restores it through the FSM, sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot from the requested index, truncates the log, and answers success
observation path: the receiver's commit index, applied index, last index and state are read through the public accessors

supporting_behavior_ids.b-install-snapshot: the installing behaviour that takes the committed state through the snapshot index as applied and stable but does not establish the commit-index fact on this path, which is the omission the question asks about
supporting_behavior_ids.b-fsm-apply: shows the applied state the installer has taken on is a consumer of the same fact on the ordinary path, which is why a published value below it is incoherent
supporting_behavior_ids.b-newraft-recovery: the second entry point of the same requirement: the startup restore publishes lastApplied and lastSnapshot from a stored snapshot and likewise leaves the commit index at zero

counterevidence: The map records the follower's commit index as min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex), which describes the append path only and can be read as defining the published value as the last advertised commit index rather than as the committed state actually held.
In a live cluster the next heartbeat carries a commit index and the append branch advances the value, so the discrepancy lasts only until the next AppendEntries reaches that follower.
The receiving node's FSM has the state either way, so an application that reads its own FSM rather than the published index is unaffected.
No in-repo consumer other than Stats was located for the value on a follower, so no internal mechanism was found that misbehaves because of it.
unknowns: whether the omission is deliberate, i.e. whether the library intends the follower's published commit index to be strictly the leader's last advertisement
which consumers outside the module rely on the value on a follower, which would raise the consequence
whether the intended repair advances the commit index inside installSnapshot or derives the published value from the last snapshot index

obligation.description: A node that installs a snapshot carrying state the source had committed and applied through index J must publish a commit context at least J: the value Raft.CommitIndex() reports may not name a commit point below the state the node has just taken as applied, because the accessor is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation.

scope.description: A node in the captured module that installs an InstallSnapshotRequest whose snapshot was produced by a leader that had committed and applied through the snapshot index, observed before any later AppendEntries advertises a commit index.
assumptions: the installed snapshot carries entries the source had committed and applied, which is what the source's own Snapshot API produces
the receiving node's last index after the install is the snapshot index, so no legal commit index exceeds it
excluded: the correctness of the snapshot payload itself, which the check does not inspect
the configuration carried by the snapshot
behaviour after a later AppendEntries has advanced the value
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

pending: which consumers rely on the published value on a follower
whether the repair advances the commit index inside installSnapshot or derives the published value from the last snapshot index
whether the startup restore path should be a second scenario of this obligation

grounding.derivation: Raft.CommitIndex() is documented as the committed index and as the basis for the read-index optimisation and returns raftState.commitIndex (s-api-commit-index). On a follower that state is otherwise advanced only in the appendEntries commit branch, which sets it to min(LeaderCommitIndex, lastIndex) and applies through processLogs (s-raft-append-commit). takeSnapshot persists the FSM at an index the node has applied (s-snapshot-take), and the payload the installer adopts is the source's committed state. installSnapshot itself publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from req.LastLogIndex and truncates the log but never writes the commit index (s-raft-install-snapshot), so the node leaves the commit index below an index it has already established as applied. The obligation therefore requires the published value to be at least the snapshot index on this path.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any node that accepts an InstallSnapshotRequest from a leader whose snapshot covers committed state. The check exercises a voter of the source's configuration installing a snapshot produced by that source's own Snapshot API, with the receiver's timers long enough that nothing else changes it inside the prefix.
unresolved: whether the published value is intentionally limited to the leader's last advertised commit index, which no source states
whether any consumer depends on the value on a follower
whether the startup restore path shares the same requirement or needs its own scenario
alternatives: the low value could be read as 'no commit index has been advertised yet', but the node has accepted and applied committed state through that index and the accessor's contract names the committed index rather than the last advertisement

bindings.description: Raft.installSnapshot streams the snapshot into a new sink, restores it through the FSM, publishes raftState.lastApplied and lastSnapshot from req.LastLogIndex, truncates the log and answers success, but never writes the commit index, so the node it leaves applied at the snapshot index publishes a lower commit index.
pending: whether the commit index should be advanced here or derived from the last snapshot index

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the publishing duty: it takes the committed state through the snapshot index as applied and stable, but leaves the index the node publishes as committed below it, and the same value is what the exported accessor and Stats report.
